title: the tester answers an exec ask over the bus with the run record of a seal-grade --exec of the command, and refuses loudly when its seal is unconfirmed
intention: The tester's public interface (the bus) carries an `exec` verb: given a literal command it runs the seal-grade `--exec` path and replies the run record, and when its own seal is unconfirmed it replies the refusal and runs nothing.
why: Measured 2026-11-19: the tester's verbs are run, notices and notice-seen (cairn/devices/tester/device.py:567). `run` takes a proof PATH and runs it at isolation none, so it is not seal-grade and cannot carry a verdict instrument, which is a literal command (outline 9.4.8.1.2). The seal-grade command run, run_exec (ticket 2c9eeab2da87), is a CLI entry only. So a box without bubblewrap (akiendell, whose verdicts for 35bb99574043 and 1eeeab70c59e exited 2 with 'cairn test --exec: refused — the instance seal is not confirmed') has nothing it can ask. Outline 9.4.8.1: such a box asks the sealer; RULE 1: the ask goes through the bus.
traces_to: Law 8 (prove, then trust: a peer's re-run of an instrument is seal-grade or it is not a proof); RULE 1 (a device's public interface is the bus); Law 7 (a refused seal stays loud).
how: A hypothesis, measured by the proof: TesterDevice.declared_verbs gains `exec` beside `run`; its handler runs run_exec's sealed path with stdout and stderr captured and replies {command, exit, timed_out, timeout_s, seconds, tail, seal_refused?} in the shape verdict.run_instrument already records. A refusal replies the exact `cairn test --exec: refused` line and runs no command. Red-first proof under cairn/devices/tester/proofs/, one tooth per clause, PROVES declared.

clauses.claim: the tester's `verbs` lists `exec`, and an `exec` ask of a passing command replies exit 0 with the record's keys command, exit, timed_out, timeout_s, seconds, tail
an `exec` ask of a failing command replies that command's own exit code and its output tail, not a refusal
an `exec` ask on a box whose seal cannot be confirmed replies the `cairn test --exec: refused` line in seal_refused, exit 2, and the command is not run (a marker file it would write does not exist)
an `exec` ask with no command, or a non-string one, is refused by name and nothing is run

decisions.text: D1: the tester answers `exec` by running the one sealed door, `cairn test --exec`, as a child process with stdout and stderr captured, and replies the record; it builds no seal of its own. Not in-process: run_exec inherits the caller's stdio and run_owned spawns on it, so capturing it in-process inside a bus handler would redirect the whole server's fd 1 and 2 under concurrent asks (measured by reading cairn/devices/tester/device.py run_exec); the child is the capture boundary.
D2: the red-first proof drives the verb through the device's declared_verbs, one tooth per clause, PROVES declared; the seal-confirmed teeth name a skip reason on a box without bwrap.

out: federated bus routing (outline 5.5.3.8, a separate intention)
